title: Redwood migration demo - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping
summary: Intro demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood. Covered endpoint mappings, prompt/template differences, embeddings, function/tool calling, streaming, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and next steps for a pilot and benchmarks.

Lucas Chen: Provision pilot account and demo workspace (sandbox) by 2026-12-09
Priya Singh: Send sample prompt sets and 95th p95 latency targets by 2026-12-12

Schedule technical POC run and follow-up check-in week of 2026-12-15
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Lawson (CTO, BrightLayer), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Samir Patel (DevOps)

Auto Summary (auto-generated style):
- Goal: Walk through how BrightLayer can migrate existing bots and embeddings pipelines from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood with minimal code changes and parity in behavior.
- Key concerns: function calling parity, streaming behavior, embeddings vector dimensional mismatches, latency & cost, VPC/private deployment for regulated data, SOC2/SAML.
- Agreed next steps: parity doc, pilot account, run benchmarks, security pack.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have about 45 minutes, so we'll run through parity mapping, show the Console, API examples, and then go into deployment and security, sound good?
[00:06] Jared Lawson: Yep that works, thanks Maya. Quick note, Samir is on for infra questions, Priya will be focused on prompt and eval stuff.
[00:12] Lucas Chen: Great, I'll jump to the demo after a quick context q: can you remind us your current stack - you're running OpenAI for chat and Together for some in-house fine-tuned models, correct?
[00:18] Priya Singh: Correct. We use OpenAI's chat for customer-facing assistants, Together for internal fine-tuned scoring models, and we've got an embeddings pipeline for semantic search on Elastic.
[00:26] Samir Patel: And infra is mostly on GCP, but we have a VPC and strict egress rules — we need VPC or private deployment for some datasets.
[00:34] Maya Patel: Thanks. Ok quick slide — high level parity mapping. The goal is minimal changes to your code: same prompt, same temperatures, map model names to Redwood model IDs, and we provide a drop-in SDK + small shim for function calling where needed.
[00:44] Maya Patel: Lucas, show the API mapping table?
[00:46] Lucas Chen: Yeah, sure — so here's a sample mapping: OpenAI chat.completions -> Redwood chat.generate endpoint, same parameters mostly, messages array, role/name, we pass through function calls; for Anthropic's completions we map to the same chat.generate but with a different model family flag. Note: Together's conv format sometimes uses different stop token semantics so we normalize that in the shim.
[01:05] Priya Singh: Stop tokens — that's been a pain, sometimes Together inserts weird tokens at end. How do you handle prompts where we rely on model-specific EOS behaviors?
[01:12] Lucas Chen: Good question. We have a normalization layer in the SDK that post-processes for known model quirks (e.g., Antiropic/Anthropic mapping, sometimes transcribed as Antiropic in our docs, sorry) and we also surface a per-model profile with subtle tokenization differences so you can tune stop sequences.
[01:27] Jared Lawson: Is that normalization happening client-side or on Redwood? We prefer client minimal changes.
[01:31] Lucas Chen: Mostly client-side shim plus model profile metadata from the control plane; so your code change is often just swapping the client import and a parameter or two — no heavy server-side rewrite.
[01:39] Samir Patel: On the network side — timelines — we need VPC peering or private deployment, what options do you have?
[01:44] Maya Patel: We have Hosted (public API with private keys), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with customer isolation), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For your use case with restricted egress and regulated data, Private is an option — we can do a VPC peering or on-prem appliance depending on your ops constraints.
[01:58] Samir Patel: Good. What's the onboarding friction and time to first inference for Private?
[02:04] Lucas Chen: For VPC-private control plane with hosted runtime in customer subnets, typical setup is 2-4 weeks for standard configs; on-prem full package can be longer depending on hardware procurement. We'll share a checklist.
[02:14] Maya Patel: Ok demo time — quick Console walkthrough. Here is the model catalog, you can see verified performance profiles, quantization options and recommended batch sizes.
[02:25] [Screen share noise — faint keyboard] Lucas Chen: Now the API demo — I'll paste an example. This is an OpenAI-style request: messages array, temperature, function call. On Redwood it's nearly identical: we accept messages, functions schema, and respond with a function_call object. Here I'm calling a small weather tool example.
[02:46] Lucas Chen: (reading) request payload: { model: "redwood-chat-1", messages: [...], functions: [...] } and the output includes streaming delta tokens; we support SSE streaming and chunked websocket streams.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Streaming behavior — does the client SDK guarantee ordering and delta events? Our frontend relies on token-level deltas for progressive render.
[03:05] Lucas Chen: Yes, we preserve ordering; deltas are same semantics as OpenAI streaming, we also include token-level meta if you opt-in for debugging. A small caveat — for some quantized model variants we do micro-batching which can introduce very small jitter at high throughput; usually under p50 latency but p95 you may see a few hundred ms extra.
[03:25] Jared Lawson: Cost question — is there a unit cost change when we move from OpenAI to Redwood? Rough numbers are ok right now.
[03:31] Maya Patel: Cost depends on model variant and quantization. We show estimates in Console and we'll provide a cost model spreadsheet. In our experience, for many open models quantized on A100 or H100 backends, customers see 20-50% token-cost reduction versus hosted competitors depending on batching and cache hit rates.
[03:49] Priya Singh: Embeddings: are dimensions the same? We use OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 right now.
[03:55] Lucas Chen: We support multiple embeddings dims and provide compatibility layers. You can choose Redwood-embedding-1024 to align or use a transformer-based 1536 dim model; we'll provide mapping and a migration script to reindex your vectors. If dims differ you'll need to re-embed or maintain dual indexes — we can help run a sampling re-embed job in the pilot.
[04:15] Samir Patel: Security — how do you do encryption and key management? KMS?
[04:18] Maya Patel: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments and for Dedicated we offer BYOK via KMS. We also have audit logs retention, RBAC, SSO via SAML/SCIM. We are SOC2 compliant and can share the security pack.
[04:30] Jared Lawson: Nice. Can you share the SOC2 and pen test reports?
[04:32] Maya Patel: Yes we'll attach security docs to the CRM record and in the next email.
[04:36] Lucas Chen: Back to parity — function/tool calling differences. A common mismatch is the function schema typing and name collisions. Our shim preserves the function JSON schema and maps the function_call.name field back to your handler. We also support tool responses as structured JSON and a fallback text response for legacy flows.
[04:55] Priya Singh: For Together models we have some custom handlers expecting a slightly different json shape. How brittle is the shim?
[05:01] Lucas Chen: We try to keep it minimal. If you have custom shapes we'll add a small adapter layer in the shim repo; many customers accept a one-file adapter.
[05:07] Maya Patel: Example migration path we propose: 1) small pilot with 10k requests/day traffic replayed to Redwood sandbox; 2) validate semantic parity with an eval set; 3) run a 2-week canary in production with dual-write or fallbacks; 4) cutover.
[05:22] Jared Lawson: Eval — how do you surface regression alerts? We need to ensure customer-facing agent doesn't degrade.
[05:27] Lucas Chen: Redwood Optimize has eval tooling — you can upload prompt sets and golden outputs, run nightly regressions, and get alerts tied to specific prompt buckets. We can wire that into your CI too.
[05:38] Samir Patel: Performance — can we run a benchmark? We're expecting 300 qps peak, with 95th latency under 350ms for short chats.
[05:46] Lucas Chen: Yes, we can. For Dedicated we'd size the GPU pool; for Hosted we'll recommend a model variant and batching policy. We'll run a benchmark using your sample payloads — we'll need your prompt templates and traffic profile.
[05:57] Maya Patel: I'll capture that as an action item.
[06:00] [Small crosstalk] Priya Singh: Quick question on logs — do you store request/response payloads by default? We need PII controls.
[06:06] Lucas Chen: By default we store minimal logs for debugging; for Private you control retention, and for Dedicated we can enable redaction on ingestion. You can also opt-out of storing payloads entirely and keep only audit metadata.
[06:18] Jared Lawson: That works. Another thing — do you support SAML SCIM provisioning for RBAC?
[06:22] Maya Patel: Yes SAML + SCIM is supported, and we can integrate with your IdP.
[06:27] Samir Patel: Any gotchas on model quantization effects on output quality? We worry about hallucination increases after quantization.
[06:33] Lucas Chen: Good point. We show per-model quality regressions in model profiles. Quantization can impact rare-token generation; for high-precision tasks we recommend higher-precision variants or mixed precision. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and flags potential quality regressions after a re-eval.
[06:49] Priya Singh: Can you do a short demo of the parity mapping for an example chat that calls a function and returns an embedding?
[06:55] Lucas Chen: Sure — I'll paste an example mapping of OpenAI -> Redwood. 
[07:00] Lucas Chen: (reads) OpenAI request: POST /v1/chat/completions body { model: "gpt-4o", messages: [...], functions: [...], function_call: "auto" } -> Redwood equivalent: POST /v1/chat.generate { model: "redwood-chat-1", messages: [...], functions: [...], tool_call: { mode: "auto" } } We provide a tiny shim that renames function_call -> tool_call and maps response.function_call to response.tool_invocation; your handler can still see the name.
[07:22] Priya Singh: That seems straightforward. For embeddings pipeline we'll need a reindex plan.
[07:27] Lucas Chen: We'll provide a migration script and a sample re-embed job. In the pilot we can run sample re-embedding for a portion of the index to estimate cost.
[07:36] Jared Lawson: Who will own the pilot infra costs?
[07:39] Maya Patel: For initial pilot we cover some compute; long-run Dedicated/Private pricing will be part of the contract. We'll share a pricing estimate.
[07:46] [Faint typing, pause] Lucas Chen: Ok I'll switch to the Optimize tab — shows recommended batching, cache TTLs, and model swap suggestions per route. You can configure automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when p95 latency is under threshold or when error rates spike.
[07:59] Priya Singh: That fallback policy is important — we need graceful degradation.
[08:03] Lucas Chen: Exactly — and we also log token-level cost breakdowns so you can attribute spend to routes.
[08:10] Jared Lawson: Any compliance for EU data residency?
[08:13] Maya Patel: Yes we support region pinning and private deployments in EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[08:20] Samir Patel: Ok next steps and responsibilities?
[08:23] Maya Patel: I'll summarize: Maya to send parity mapping CSV + sample shims + pricing by Tuesday 2026-12-08; Lucas to provision a sandbox pilot and share account details by 2026-12-09; Priya to send prompt sets and target metrics by 2026-12-12; schedule POC check-in week of 2026-12-15.
[08:40] Priya Singh: Sounds good, please include a checklist for VPC peering info.
[08:44] Maya Patel: Will do. Any final Qs?
[08:46] Jared Lawson: No, that's it for me. Thanks everyone.
[08:49] Maya Patel: Great thanks, we'll follow up with next steps and the security pack.
[08:53] Lucas Chen: Thanks all, bye.

Notes about transcription quality: Some model names were mistranscribed (e.g., Antiropic for Anthropic) and K-V cache spoken as K-V cash in places. There are occasional overlaps and filler words retained to preserve meeting cadence.
